annotations.text:
1 · First run
The whole primary job: name it, pick a version, go. No repo, no Git, no config file — those come later and only when asked for.

2 · Setting up
Real named stages, and the address and password shown before it's ready. Ends by telling you the next one takes 9 seconds, not 40.

3 · Odoo & databases — the centre of the app
Both shapes, visible at once: one server holding several databases, and a database with a server to itself. Odoo's addons_path is per-server, so the rule is real, not cosmetic.

4 · A database
Address, login, password, size, last backup. Everything a junior needs on one screen; modules, code and logs are tabs, not the front door.

5 · New database
The shared-vs-own-server decision is made for you and explained in one sentence, with an escape hatch. Nobody should have to learn addons_path to make a second database.

6 · Engine
No Docker: bundled Python runtime per Odoo version, a private Postgres, a pinned PDF binary. One folder, no daemon, no admin password — and an honest note about the one fragile piece.

7 · Editor
The rail answers the two questions you actually have while coding: which database am I hitting, and how do I make this change take effect.
